s:
Campanian Cicerchia Soup

Campi Flegrei grass-pea soup with guanciale, aromatic vegetables, white wine, cherry tomatoes, and chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 cups dried cicerchie or grass peas
about 3/4 cup finely chopped guanciale
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
3 carrots, finely chopped
1 onion, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 small chile
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1 1/3 cups halved cherry tomatoes
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 1/8 qt cold water for the first cooking
3 cups plus 3 tbsp reserved cicerchia cooking liquid for the second stage
1 1/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Check the cicerchie and remove any small stones.

2. Soak in plenty of warm water for 24–48 hours.

3. Change the soaking water at least twice.

4. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

5. Put the cicerchie in a pot with the cold unsalted water.

6. Bring to a boil.

7. Cook over moderate heat for about 2 hours, until tender but not falling apart.

8. Drain only immediately before the final preparation, reserving the measured cooking liquid.

9. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

10. Add the guanciale, celery, carrots, onion, and garlic.

11. Brown for 8–10 minutes.

12. Pour in the white wine.

13. Let the alcohol evaporate.

14. Add the cicerchie.

15. Pour in the reserved cooking liquid.

16. Bring to a gentle simmer.

17. Cook over low heat for about 50 minutes.

18. Add the tomatoes, chile, and salt.

19. Continue for another 10 minutes.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Add the salt only near the end so it does not slow the softening of the cicerchie during their long cooking.

Pasta and Potato Soup

Creamy pasta-and-potato soup with scallion, carrot, celery, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 3 cups small soup pasta
1 scallion, finely chopped
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
about 2 2/3 cups diced peeled potatoes
3 cups water
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper, optional
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano, optional

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan.

2. Add the scallion, carrot, and celery.

3. Sauté for 2–3 minutes.

4. Add the potatoes.

5. Cook for another 3 minutes.

6. Add the water.

7. Add the salt.

8. Bring to a boil.

9. Cook for 3 minutes.

10. Add the pasta.

11. Cook for the package time, stirring frequently.

12. During the final 5 minutes, mash several potato cubes against the side of the pot to make the broth creamy.

13. Add the pepper if using.

Service

Rest for 2 minutes and serve with Parmigiano if desired.

Chef's note

Stir frequently while the pasta cooks so the concentrated starch at the bottom does not cause the soup to stick.

Cabbage and Rice Soup

Neapolitan Savoy-cabbage-and-rice soup with pork ribs, onion, garlic, and Parmigiano rind.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 medium Savoy cabbage, about 2 1/4 lb
1 onion, sliced
1 1/3 cups Carnaroli or Arborio rice
2 meaty pork ribs, about 1 1/8 lb
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 garlic clove
1 piece Parmigiano rind, about 1/3 cup
2 2/3 qt water
2 tsp fine salt, divided
1 cup hot broth, available if needed for the pork

Preparation

1. Clean the cabbage.

2. Wash, drain, and tear the leaves into pieces.

3. Bring the water to a boil.

4. Add about 1 1/3 teaspoons salt.

5. Add the cabbage.

6. Cook for 30 minutes.

7. Add the Parmigiano rind.

8. When the water returns to a boil, add the rice.

9. Stir well.

10. Cook for about 30 minutes, or until the rice is tender.

11. Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a skillet.

12. Add the garlic, onion, and pork ribs cut into pieces.

13. Brown for 10 minutes.

14. Reduce the heat.

15. Cook until the pork is tender, about 30 minutes, adding hot broth in 1/4-cup portions if the pan becomes dry.

16. Remove the garlic.

17. Drain the rice and cabbage, reserving 1 cup of their cooking liquid.

18. Transfer to a serving bowl.

19. Add the pork and its pan juices.

20. Add the reserved cooking liquid to achieve a soup consistency.

21. Add the remaining salt only if needed.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Reserving some cabbage-and-rice cooking liquid lets you adjust the final consistency without diluting the flavor.

Lucanian Chickpea Soup

Basilicata chickpea-and-pearled-wheat soup with carrot, celery, onion, garlic, bay, and rosemary.

Yield: 4–6 servings

Ingredients

1 1/4 cups dried chickpeas
1 cup pearled wheat berries
1 carrot, about 3/4 cup diced
1 celery stalk, about 1/2 cup diced
1 onion, about 1 cup diced
1 garlic clove
1 bay leaf
1 small rosemary sprig
6 1/3 cups hot water or light vegetable broth
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 tbsp finely chopped fresh parsley
1 1/4 tsp fine salt, divided
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 small dried chile, optional

Preparation

1. Soak the chickpeas overnight.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the chickpeas in a pot.

4. Cover with fresh water.

5. Bring slowly to a boil.

6. Skim.

7. Cook over low heat for 60–90 minutes.

8. Add half of the salt during the final 15 minutes.

9. Drain, reserving 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons cooking liquid.

10. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

11. Add the garlic and rosemary.

12. Add the carrot, celery, and onion.

13. Cook for about 8 minutes.

14. Rinse the wheat.

15. Add it to the saucepan.

16. Stir for 2 minutes.

17. Add 4 1/4 cups hot water or broth.

18. Add the bay leaf.

19. Cook for 30–40 minutes.

20. Add the chickpeas.

21. Add 1 cup reserved chickpea liquid.

22. Continue for 15–20 minutes.

23. If the soup becomes too thick, add the remaining reserved liquid.

24. Remove the garlic, rosemary, and bay leaf.

25. Add the remaining salt and pepper.

26. Rest for 5 minutes.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil, parsley, and optional chile.

Chef's note

The wheat continues absorbing liquid while resting; turn off the heat while the soup is slightly looser than the final texture you want.

Crapiata Materana

Matera mixed-legume-and-grain soup with new potatoes, tomato, bay, chile, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1/2 cup whole dried fava beans
1/2 cup farro
1/2 cup dried chickpeas
1/2 cup dried cicerchie or grass peas
1/2 cup dried peas
1/2 cup dried white beans
1/2 cup dried black-eyed peas
1 cup small lentils
1 cup durum wheat berries
6 small new potatoes
1 carrot
1 celery stalk
1 onion
4 cherry tomatoes
2 bay leaves
3 1/4 qt water, plus 4 1/4 cups available if needed
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp ground chile
6 slices toasted bread

Preparation

1. The day before, soak all of the dried legumes and grains in plenty of water for 24 hours.

2. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

3. Wash the new potatoes without peeling them.

4. Put the legumes, grains, and potatoes in a large pot.

5. Add the water.

6. Bring to a gentle simmer.

7. Cook over low heat for about 45 minutes.

8. Add the whole carrot, celery stalk, and onion.

9. Cut the cherry tomatoes into pieces.

10. Add them with the bay leaves and half of the salt.

11. Cook for another 45 minutes.

12. Stir every 15 minutes.

13. If the liquid drops below the legumes before they are tender, add the reserved water in 1-cup portions.

14. Remove the carrot, celery, onion, and bay leaves.

15. Add the remaining salt.

Service

Finish with olive oil, chile, and toasted bread.

Chef's note

Different legumes and grains absorb water at different rates; adding any extra water only in measured portions keeps the crapiata thick rather than watery.

Fava Bean and Chicory Soup

Lucanian dried-fava purée with wild chicory sautéed with garlic and chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/2 cups dried fava beans
about 12 cups field chicory or catalogna
2 garlic cloves
1 small hot chile, sliced
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 1/8 qt water for the fava beans
3 1/4 qt water for the chicory
1 2/3 tsp fine salt, divided

Preparation

1. Rinse the fava beans.

2. Soak in plenty of warm water overnight.

3. Drain.

4. Put the fava beans in a pot with the fresh water.

5. Bring to a gentle simmer.

6. Cook until completely soft, about 60–90 minutes.

7. Add about 2/3 teaspoon salt during the final 15 minutes.

8. Drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid.

9. Blend the fava beans until smooth, adding only enough reserved liquid to make a creamy purée.

10. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil with 1 garlic clove and half of the chile.

11. Add the purée.

12. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

13. Clean and wash the chicory.

14. Bring the measured water to a boil with about 2/3 teaspoon salt.

15. Boil the chicory for 10–15 minutes, until tender.

16. Drain and squeeze dry.

17. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a second skillet.

18. Add the remaining garlic and chile.

19. Add the chicory.

20. Sauté for 5 minutes.

21. Add the remaining salt.

Service

Spoon the fava purée onto plates, add the chicory alongside, and finish with the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

The fava purée should be thick but not dry; using its own cooking liquid preserves both flavor and starch.

Mashing only part of the beans thickens the soup while preserving whole pieces and a rustic texture.

Calabrian red Tropea onion cream soup with tomato, Parmigiano, basil, and mullet bottarga.

2/3 cup tomato passata

14 tbsp butter
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
10 basil leaves

about 3 tbsp finely grated or thinly sliced mullet bottarga

1. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot.

2. Add the onions.

3. Add half of the salt.

5. Add the tomato passata.

10. Add the remaining broth.

11. Continue for another 10–20 minutes, until the onions are completely soft.

12. Add the Parmigiano.

13. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth.

14. Add the remaining salt and pepper.

15. Return to low heat for 2 minutes.

Service

Divide among bowls and finish with basil and bottarga.

Chef's note

Cooking the onions slowly without browning preserves the characteristic sweetness of Tropea onions and keeps the soup's flavor clean.

about 15 cups chard
1 large carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1 small onion, finely chopped
about 1/2 cup dried mushrooms
1 tbsp tomato paste
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
6 1/3 cups hot water
1 rosemary sprig
1 garlic clove
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Soak the chickpeas in plenty of cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the chickpeas in a pot with fresh water.

4. Simmer until tender, about 90–120 minutes.

5. Reserve 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons chickpea cooking liquid.

6. Soak the dried mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes.

7. Drain, reserving 1/2 cup soaking liquid.

8. Strain the mushroom liquid very carefully.

9. Chop the mushrooms.

10. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

11. Add the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, and rosemary.

12. Cook for 8 minutes.

13. Add the mushrooms.

14. Add the tomato paste.

15. Cook for 2 minutes.

16. Add the strained mushroom liquid.

17. Add the chard cut into strips.

18. Cover.

19. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes.

20. Add the chickpeas.

21. Add the hot water and 1 cup chickpea cooking liquid.

22. Add the salt and pepper.

23. Cook for about 30 minutes.

24. If the soup is too thick, add the remaining chickpea liquid.

25. Remove the garlic and rosemary.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

The strained mushroom soaking liquid concentrates the flavor of the zemin; filter it very carefully so no grit enters the soup.

Bagnun di Acciughe

Liguria anchovy soup with fresh anchovies, tomato, onion, garlic, white wine, and sailor crackers.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb very fresh anchovies
3 1/3 cups peeled tomatoes or peeled grape tomatoes, chopped
1 onion, thinly sliced
1 garlic clove, crushed
1/2 cup dry white wine
1/4 cup Ligurian extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1/2 cup water
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 1/4 tsp fine salt
6 sailor crackers or 6 thick toast slices

Preparation

1. Clean the anchovies, removing the heads and innards.

2. Rinse briefly.

3. Drain on paper towels.

4. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a wide saucepan.

5. Add the onion and garlic.

6. Cook over medium-low heat for 5–6 minutes.

7. Remove the garlic.

8. Pour in the wine.

9. Let the alcohol evaporate for 2 minutes.

10. Add the tomatoes.

11. Add the water.

12. Add the salt.

13. Cook for about 15 minutes.

14. Add the anchovies in an even layer.

15. Cover.

16. Immediately turn off the heat.

17. Rest for 10 minutes; the residual heat will cook the anchovies.

18. Add the parsley.

19. Put one sailor cracker in each bowl.

20. Drizzle the crackers with the remaining olive oil.

Service

Spoon the anchovies, tomatoes, and plenty of broth over the crackers.

Chef's note

After adding the anchovies, turn off the heat so they stay moist and cook gently in the residual heat of the soup.

Jota

Trieste bean-and-sauerkraut soup with smoked pork ribs, pancetta, and potatoes.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups dried beans, soaked overnight
about 2 cups plus 2 tbsp sauerkraut
2 smoked pork ribs
about 3/4 cup sliced pancetta
4 potatoes, diced
1/2 onion, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, minced
2 bay leaves
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 2/3 qt water, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt, only if needed

Preparation

1. Drain and rinse the soaked beans.

2. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

3. Add the pancetta and 1 bay leaf.

4. Brown for 4–5 minutes.

5. Add the onion and garlic.

6. Cook for another 5 minutes.

7. Rinse the sauerkraut lightly if it is very sour.

8. Squeeze dry.

9. Add it to the saucepan.

10. Add 4 1/4 cups water.

11. Cover.

12. Cook over low heat for 1 hour.

13. Meanwhile, put the beans in another pot.

14. Add the smoked ribs and second bay leaf.

15. Add 6 1/3 cups water.

16. Bring to a boil.

17. Cook over low heat for 1 hour.

18. Uncover the sauerkraut.

19. Cook over higher heat for another 30 minutes, until the liquid reduces.

20. Add the potatoes to the beans.

21. Cook for 30 minutes.

22. Remove the ribs and bay leaf.

23. Blend about one-third of the beans and potatoes with some of their broth.

24. Return the purée to the pot.

25. Add the sauerkraut.

26. Remove the meat from the ribs and return it to the jota.

27. Cook together for 10 minutes.

28. Taste and add the salt only if needed.

Service

Rest for 10 minutes and serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Smoked ribs, pancetta, and sauerkraut are already quite salty, so add salt only after the final combination.

Minestra de Bobici

Trieste fresh-corn-and-bean soup with potatoes, lard, celery, garlic, and a light flour roux.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 3 cups shelled fresh beans or soaked dried beans
3 ears sweet corn
2 potatoes, diced
about 2/3 cup finely chopped lard
2 tbsp olive oil
2 celery leaves, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, minced
3 tbsp all-purpose flour
6 1/3 cups water, divided
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. If using dried beans, soak for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the beans in a pot with 4 1/4 cups water.

4. Add half of the salt and the pepper.

5. Bring to a gentle simmer.

6. Cook for at least 1 hour, until tender.

7. Cut the kernels from the corn.

8. Put the kernels in a second pot with 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons water.

9. Bring to a boil.

10. Cook until the outer skins are tender, about 20–30 minutes.

11. Drain the corn, reserving 1 cup of its cooking water.

12. Add the potatoes to the beans.

13. Cook for 15–20 minutes, until tender.

14. Put the lard, olive oil, celery leaves, and garlic in a small skillet.

15. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

16. Add the flour.

17. Stir for 2 minutes to make a lightly golden roux.

18. Gradually whisk in the reserved corn cooking water.

19. Pour the roux into the bean pot.

20. Add the cooked corn.

21. Cook together for 2–3 minutes.

22. Add the remaining salt only if needed.

Service

Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm.

Chef's note

Diluting the roux with the corn cooking water before adding it to the soup prevents lumps and preserves the corn flavor.

Caprese Salad

Classic Caprese salad with buffalo mozzarella, ripe tomatoes, basil, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 2 servings

Ingredients

about 2 cups sliced buffalo mozzarella
2 large ripe tomatoes
10 fresh basil leaves
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/3 tsp fine sea salt

Preparation

1. Drain the mozzarella.

2. Pat it gently dry with paper towels.

3. Cut into slices about 3/8 inch thick.

4. Wash and dry the tomatoes.

5. Cut them into slices the same thickness as the mozzarella.

6. Arrange alternating tomato and mozzarella slices on a platter.

7. Tuck the basil leaves between the slices.

8. Sprinkle with the salt.

9. Drizzle evenly with the olive oil.

Service

Serve immediately at room temperature.

Chef's note

Cutting the tomatoes and mozzarella to the same thickness creates a balanced flavor and texture in every bite.
